baseline.name: DFS with separate visited grid
baseline.approach: Flood-fill each unvisited land component using an explicit visited matrix.
baseline.space: O(m*n) visited storage and worst-case traversal stack

archived.name: Recursive sink-in-place DFS
archived.space: O(m*n) worst-case recursive stack; no visited matrix

why: Changing visited land to water removes the separate visited grid while preserving once-per-cell exploration.
quantitative_comparison: One m-by-n visited matrix is avoided, but worst-case auxiliary growth remains O(m*n) because recursion can reach every land cell. No asymptotic total-space or elapsed-time superiority is established.
tradeoffs: The input map is destroyed, and a large connected island can exhaust the stack. An iterative traversal can provide better stack control.
evidence_basis: Static comparison isolating the avoided visited allocation, with recursion costs retained; no timing benchmark.
